title: Infosys Signs 10-Year AI Deal to Overhaul Crocs' Enterprise Systems
excerpt: The Bengaluru-headquartered IT services giant will deploy AI-first solutions across the footwear brand's operations, aiming to unify data silos and enable real-time decision-making.
body:
• Infosys has entered a 10-year strategic agreement with Crocs Inc. to deliver AI-first solutions across the footwear company's IT and business operations.
  • The deal aims to break down operational silos, unify data across the organisation and enable real-time, insight-driven decision-making.
  • Crocs is already using agentic AI for dynamic product recommendations and has partnered with AI platform Ablo for custom Jibbitz charm design.
  • The partnership follows a similar 10-year AI transformation deal Infosys signed with HanesBrands in 2025.

Infosys has signed a 10-year strategic partnership with American footwear brand Crocs Inc. to modernise the company's core business and IT systems using artificial intelligence, the companies announced on Wednesday.

Under the agreement, the Bengaluru-based IT services and consulting firm will deploy scalable, AI-first solutions across Crocs' enterprise IT and business operations. The deal is designed to break down operational silos, unify data across the organisation and enable real-time decision-making — a playbook Infosys has been running with increasing frequency across the retail sector.

Reimagining IT From the Ground Up

"By leveraging Infosys' proven delivery frameworks and advanced automation capabilities, we will optimise operations, reduce costs and scale responsibly — while driving continuous improvement and building a foundation for sustainable growth."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PNUIZ3w1GUs — Tom Britt, CIO, Crocs Inc.

Crocs has already been pushing the envelope on technology adoption. The company has deployed agentic AI to read customers in real time and dynamically adjust product recommendations. It has also collaborated with AI fashion design platform Ablo to let customers design one-of-a-kind Jibbitz charms, and last year unveiled a new experiential store concept featuring immersive storytelling and personalisation.

The Infosys partnership takes that ambition to the enterprise layer, targeting the back-end systems that power supply chain, inventory, finance and human resources.

Infosys' Retail AI Playbook

The Crocs deal follows a strikingly similar agreement Infosys signed with HanesBrands in 2025 — also a 10-year AI transformation partnership. In both cases, the company deploys its Live Enterprise Automation Platform (LEAP) integrated with Infosys Topaz, its suite of AI-first services built on generative AI and AIOps capabilities.

"The retail industry is at an unprecedented inflection point, where new AI-augmented digital imaginations can be industrialised rapidly."

— Karmesh Vaswani, EVP & Global Head, Consumer, Retail & Logistics, Infosys

For Infosys, such deals represent a strategic hedge against fears that AI will cannibalise traditional IT outsourcing revenue. By positioning itself as the partner that deploys AI rather than the labour force AI replaces, the company is attempting to stay ahead of the disruption curve. AI-related services generated revenue of approximately ₹25 billion — about 5.5 percent of total revenue — in its most recent December quarter.

What It Means for India's IT Sector

The deal underscores a broader trend: Indian IT services companies are locking in long-duration AI transformation contracts to build revenue visibility. Tata Consultancy Services has reported about $1.8 billion in annual AI services revenue, while Wipro and HCLTech have been repositioning as transformation partners.

For the Indian diaspora tech workforce, these mega-deals signal that AI expertise — rather than volume staffing — is becoming the primary currency. The companies winning these contracts are those with demonstrable AI platforms, not just headcount. As Crocs, HanesBrands and others bet their IT futures on decade-long AI overhauls, the demand for specialised talent in generative AI, AIOps and enterprise automation is set to intensify.
